A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReAG research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReAG evaluations on Encyclopedic-VQA and InfoSeek, component ablations, retrieval analyses, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds passage-filtering recall and specificity results in Table 6.

M1.justification: The retrieval pipeline, critic, SFT/RL objectives, generator, and prompts remain unchanged. The empty-context behavior emphasized in v2 was already documented in v1 Appendix D.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same datasets and retrieval/evidence scenarios, including oracle documents and Google Lens retrieval. The new filtering analysis uses existing E-VQA coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 6 compares filtering against three ReflectiVA variants, including Qwen2.5-VL-7B, which was absent from the passage-count comparison in Figure 3(right). The main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 6 introduces passage-level recall and specificity evaluation on E-VQA, supplementing retained-passage counts and answer accuracy. Existing splits, training settings, and benchmark evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new filtering analysis directly examines evidence retention and irrelevant-passage rejection. Existing component ablations, retrieval-depth and threshold sweeps, training curves, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: There are no changes to run-count, seed, uncertainty, or significance reporting. Table 6 adds classification performance estimates, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 6 newly reports ReAG recall/specificity of 94.6/95.7, versus 91.3/93.8 for ReflectiVA with the matching Qwen2.5-VL-3B backbone, alongside other ReflectiVA results. Existing results remain unchanged; C.4's 40.2 and 27.1 repeat Table 4.

T1.justification: The task formulation, equations 1–9, and Appendix B reward definitions are mathematically unchanged. No new assumptions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about retrieval filtering, reinforcement-learning-based reasoning, accuracy, and interpretability. The appendix additions support existing contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix C.4 attributes gains partly to evidence quality, explains the role of distractor training, and links evidence-absent results partly to the fallback-context difference from ReflectiVA. Appendix F's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Page 1 replaces the explicit public-source-code statement and direct repository link with a project-homepage link. C.4 newly describes ReflectiVA's random-passage fallback; ReAG's empty-context handling and negative-sampling proportions were already disclosed.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Related Work section remain unchanged. Appendix C.4 adds a specific distinction from ReflectiVA concerning random fallback passages, modestly refining comparative positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes small introductory edits, adds an equal-contribution note, and expands appendix discussion. The former C.4 Critic Threshold subsection becomes a paragraph within C.3, while a new C.4 discusses performance gains.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6, makes small typographical adjustments to Figure 2, and reflows the first page and appendix prompt boxes. Existing experimental displays retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: Table 6 strengthens the filtering argument by measuring evidence retention and rejection directly, beyond v1's passage-count analysis. Appendix C.4 also clarifies the fallback difference affecting interpretation of evidence-absent results. These are useful, limited improvements; the new table's evaluation construction remains sparsely documented, and the central results and method are unchanged.
